title: Find Winner on a Tic Tac Toe Game
statement:
Two players, A and B, play tic-tac-toe on a 3 x 3 board that starts empty. A goes first and writes `X`, B writes `O`, they alternate turns, and a mark may only go into an empty cell. Play stops the moment one player holds all three cells of some row, column or either diagonal (that player wins), or once all nine cells are filled.

`moves[i] = [row, col]` is the cell marked on turn `i` (counting from 0, so even `i` belongs to A). Return `"A"` or `"B"` for the winner, `"Draw"` when the board is full and nobody won, and `"Pending"` when nobody has won yet but empty cells remain.

`moves` is always a legal game: no cell is used twice and no move is made after the game is over.
constraints: No cell appears twice in moves
moves is a legal game: A starts and no move follows the end of the game
notes:
## Intuition

The direct way is to fill a 3 x 3 grid with the moves and then inspect all eight lines. A lighter simulation keeps one running tally per line: A adds `+1`, B adds `-1`. A line reaches `+3` or `-3` exactly when one player owns all of it, so after each move only the lines through that cell can have just been completed. Because a legal game stops at the first win, the first move that pushes a tally to 3 in absolute value decides the winner.

## Approach

1. Keep tallies `rows`, `cols`, `diagonal` (cells with `row === col`) and `antiDiagonal` (cells with `row + col === 2`).
2. Walk through the moves. Turn `i` belongs to A when `i` is even, so `mark` is `+1` for A and `-1` for B.
3. Add `mark` to the row and column of the cell, and to each diagonal the cell lies on.
4. If any of those tallies now has absolute value 3, return the player who made this move.
5. With no winner, return `"Draw"` after 9 moves and `"Pending"` otherwise.

## Example 1, step by step

`moves = [[0,0],[2,0],[1,1],[2,1],[2,2]]`.
- A at `(0,0)`: `rows[0] = 1`, `cols[0] = 1`, `diagonal = 1`.
- B at `(2,0)`: `rows[2] = -1`, `cols[0] = 0`, `antiDiagonal = -1`.
- A at `(1,1)`: `rows[1] = 1`, `cols[1] = 1`, `diagonal = 2`, `antiDiagonal = 0`.
- B at `(2,1)`: `rows[2] = -2`, `cols[1] = 0`.
- A at `(2,2)`: `rows[2] = -1`, `cols[2] = 1`, `diagonal = 3`, so `won` is true and the answer is `"A"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m), where m ≤ 9 is the number of moves; each move updates at most four tallies.
- Space: O(1): eight numbers for a 3 x 3 board.

## Pitfalls

- The centre cell `(1,1)` lies on both diagonals, so test the two diagonal conditions separately rather than with `else`.
- A full board can still have a winner; check for a win before answering `"Draw"`.
- Fewer than 9 moves with no winner is `"Pending"`, not `"Draw"`, even when nobody can win any more.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rows`, `cols` | tally of each row and column (A counts `+1`, B `-1`) |
| `diagonal`, `antiDiagonal` | tallies of the two diagonals |
| `i` | turn number; even turns are A's |
| `row`, `col` | the cell marked on this turn |
| `mark` | `+1` for A, `-1` for B |
| `won` | whether this move completed a line |

narration.2: One tally per row: A adds 1, B subtracts 1.
narration.3: One tally per column, kept the same way.
narration.4: Tally for the main diagonal, where row equals column.
narration.5: Tally for the other diagonal, where row + col is 2.
narration.7: Replay the moves in the order they were played.
narration.8: Read the cell marked on this turn.
narration.9: Even turns are A's (+1), odd turns are B's (-1).
narration.10: Count the mark in its row...
narration.12: Is the cell on the main diagonal?
narration.15: Is the cell on the other diagonal? The centre is on both.
narration.16: Then count it there as well.
narration.18: A tally of 3 or -3 means one player owns that whole line.
narration.20: The player who made this move wins.
narration.23: No winner: a full board is a draw, otherwise the game is still going.
